title: Leave Planner
overviewHtml:
Who plans to be away and who is actually away, day by day for one month, grouped by organization unit. It opens on the current month; the arrows move a month back or forward.

Each unit has a line of its own showing how many of its people are away, or planning to be, on each day; below it is one line per employee, coloured by what falls on the day: Planned - Approved, Planned - Open, Leave - Approved and Leave - Open. A day can carry more than one, because a plan sitting on top of approved leave is exactly the thing to spot. Hover over a day for the details. Only employees with something in the month get a line, and each employee sits under the unit they are assigned to today; those in no unit come last, under No department.

Plans come from Leave Planner Request in self-service and book nothing; leave comes from the employees' leave records. Hourly absences are left out — they are short permissions, not days away. Drafts never show, and neither do rejected, withdrawn or cancelled plans and leave.

fields.label: Dashboard_Showing
fields.html:
What it is. The line in the toolbar that says whose data the dashboard is built from, and how many employees that is. You never choose it: it follows from who you are.

How it is worked out. The employees you see are:

  • everyone, if you hold the Admin role;
  • otherwise the employees in the organization units given to your roles in row-level security, including every unit below them, plus your own team — you and everybody below you in the manager hierarchy, at every level;
  • nobody, if neither gives anyone. The dashboard then shows nothing, never everything.

Example. "Showing: Finance + Payroll + your team (123 employees)" — you are an HR officer for Finance and Payroll, and also manage a team of your own.

Why it matters. Two people can open the same dashboard and see different numbers, and both are right. Every figure, chart, list and download on the page is limited to these employees — changing a filter can narrow them further but never widen them.
fields.adminHtml: Resolved by IDashboardScopeService for every dashboard. The row-level security on/off switch in Security Settings is deliberately not consulted: with nothing assigned the user sees nothing, whatever the switch says. The Admin rule matches the static tenant role name Admin.

fields.label: OrganizationUnit
fields.html:
What it is. Narrows the planner to one unit and every unit below it. All shows everybody you can see.

Example. Finance — which also shows Finance / Payroll and Finance / Accounts.

Why it matters. The list offers only the units your employees sit in, so choosing one never empties the list of the others.

fields.label: Employee
fields.html:
What it is. Narrows the planner to employees whose code, English name or Arabic name contains the text. Press Enter to apply it.

Example. Ahmed

fields.label: ShowActualLeaveApproved
fields.html: What it is. Shows leave that is in effect: approved, or recorded without approval. On when the planner opens.

fields.label: ShowActualLeaveUnapproved
fields.html: What it is. Shows leave still waiting with an approver. Leave that was rejected or sent back is not shown.

fields.label: ShowLeavePlannerApproved
fields.html: What it is. Shows leave plans that are in effect: approved, or recorded without approval. On when the planner opens.

fields.label: ShowLeavePlannerUnapproved
fields.html:
What it is. Shows leave plans still waiting with an approver.

Why it matters. Together with approved leave, it shows what managers are about to be asked to agree to while there is still time to plan cover.
